Privacy notice

This site is built to know as little about you as possible. Here is exactly what happens when you visit it.

Summary

  • No cookies, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking pixels, no fingerprinting, no session recording. One optional browser-storage entry if you use the light/dark toggle (see below).
  • No contact form, no comment system, no embedded social-media widgets, no third-party fonts or scripts.
  • The only data processing that happens when you visit is the hosting provider's own server logging (below).
  • If you email me, I use your address and message to reply, and for nothing else.

Who is responsible

This website is published by Alexandros Kaminas, a researcher based in the Netherlands, in a personal and professional capacity. It is not a business and offers nothing for sale. For anything concerning your personal data on this site, contact me at kaminas.alex@gmail.com.

Hosting and server logs

The site is a set of static files served by GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc. (San Francisco, USA) and, for users in the EU, GitHub B.V. (Amsterdam). According to GitHub's documentation, when a GitHub Pages site is visited, the visitor's IP address is logged and stored by GitHub for security purposes, whether or not the visitor is signed in to GitHub. GitHub performs this logging for its own purposes under its own privacy statement; I do not receive, see or control these logs, and GitHub does not publish a retention period for them. GitHub states that it relies on EU standard contractual clauses and its certification under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for transfers of personal data to the United States.

Details: GitHub Pages data collection and the GitHub Privacy Statement.

To the extent that I am regarded as a controller for this processing, the legal basis is legitimate interest (GDPR Article 6(1)(f)): running a professional website on infrastructure that is kept secure. No other data is collected on my behalf.

Cookies and local storage

This site sets no cookies and does not use session storage or IndexedDB. It loads no third-party scripts, fonts, images or embeds; all requests go to this site's own domain.

The colour scheme follows your operating-system preference. If you use the sun/moon button in the header to choose the other scheme, that choice is kept in your browser's local storage under a single entry namedtheme, which records only the scheme name and the time you chose it. It is stored only while your choice differs from your system setting (switching back removes it), it expires after 180 days, it contains nothing that identifies you, and it never leaves your browser. Nothing else is stored, and nothing is stored at all unless you use that button. Because this is a preference you set yourself, no consent banner is shown.

This was verified on the deployed site in a clean browser profile (see the compliance notes in the source repository). If that ever changes, this notice will be updated first.

If you email me

The contact link opens your own email program. When you write to me I receive your email address, anything you include in the message, and the technical headers your mail provider adds. I use these to reply and to keep track of our correspondence, on the basis of your request (GDPR Article 6(1)(b)) or my legitimate interest in answering professional enquiries (Article 6(1)(f)). Messages are kept as long as the correspondence is relevant and then deleted. My mailbox is provided by Google (Gmail); Google's own privacy terms apply to the transport and storage of mail.

External links

The site links to external services: GitHub, ORCID, Google Scholar, ResearchGate, the University of Groningen research portal, DOI resolvers and publishers. These are ordinary links, not embeds; nothing is loaded from them until you choose to follow one. Their privacy policies apply once you leave this site.

Your rights

Under the GDPR you have the right to access, rectify or erase personal data concerning you, to restrict or object to its processing, and to data portability where applicable. In practice the only personal data I hold about visitors is email correspondence, which I will show you, correct or delete on request. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority; in the Netherlands this is the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens. For server logs held by GitHub, please contact GitHub directly through its privacy statement.
